Dagur Asgeirsson said:

Now only some errors towards the end of the TwoTruncated file need to be fixed. The issue is that ReflQuiv.adj was refactored.

@Marcelo Lynch and Claude have bumped mathlib further (on the same PR). But the sorries remain. Who's the expert in the TwoTruncated file?

Hi! Now that the repo is close to the tip of mathlib again, I think it might be worth incorporating the downstream-reports automation.

cosmos#171 is this change. The new automation replaces the current one (which is opening PRs like cosmos#170 and issues like cosmos#132): the behavior is similar but richer: when there is a breaking change in mathlib, the opened issue
will say exactly which (mathlib) commit is the one that introduced the break, and the repo will also get a PR bumping to that exact commit (which shouldn't be merged -- it's meant to produce a branch that one can check out and fix in place).

Here are examples of this from FLT:

  • FLT#1004 ('bump to latest' when the latest is compatible)
  • FLT#1007 ('bump mathlib ... fix breaking changes') - notice the manual intervention here, and the description pointing to the culprit
  • FLT#1008 - the associated issue when something breaks

We've fallen behind the master branch again and I'm having an unusually busy summer, so haven't been able to figure out the issue. There's an issue created by @Alejandro Soto Franco here that contains some diagnostics. But see also a previous issue which highlights a bunch of errors caused by some mathlib bump.

If anyone here has a moment to look in to this, I'd appreciate it. Otherwise I think it's likely I won't have a chance to investigate until early September...
(Similarly, I've also been very delayed in reviewing a number of other open PRs. If someone else has the capacity to help reviewing, that would be great as well.)

cosmos#132 (the 'previous issue' you link above) should be closed, it's from 2025 and is not relevant any longer.

These automated issues / PRs for bumping mathlib are now handled by the Update Dependencies, but as cosmos#202 describes, this automation is currently tripped by the fact that the v4.32.2 version is not part of the "linear history" of mathlib (it's a patch, .2, off v4.32.0), so it can't really 'scan' the history to pinpoint a breaking change.

I'll look into ways of supporting this scenario more gracefully from the automation (at least with better reporting).

In the meantime, we should try to get the repo back to some version of 'master' so that these scans can work again, and then resume bumping 'atomically'. Here's a bump to v4.33.0, which includes the kernel fixes that prompted the .2 patches: cosmos#209
Thanks @Marcelo Lynch I was a bit puzzled on how to handle the version history, appreciate the support
I'll dispatch a downstream-reports run once cosmos#209 merges to identify the next bump (and fix "Update Dependencies")

Also, feel free to ping me directly about issues or quirks around downstream-reports (i.e., these 'bump' issues / PRs), I'm always looking on ways to improve the system and accommodate to downstream maintainers' workflows.

cosmos#210 bumps to the latest mathlib (with minor fixes), but notably adds --wfail to the CI (and also cleans the warnings). This will make further warnings fail the CI build, which I would say is good practice but it's probably not my decision to make :-)
I'm very happy to be advised by good practice because I seldom know what is best! Thanks for your help @Marcelo Lynch

One consequence of --wfail is that it will fail the build on sorry warnings too. I don't know if its typical for infinity-cosmos to check-in sorries.

Another thing to consider is to include these options in the lakefile.toml's [leanOptions]:

[leanOptions]
...
#  Fail a module upon warnings:
warningAsError = true

# Do not emit warnings when encountering sorry
# The blueprint tracks this anyways
warn.sorry = false

This makes anyone building locally also encounter failures-on-warnings and not just the CI. Arguably it makes for a better contribution/review experience.
We have checked in sorries in the past but are not doing so currently. I'm okay with not having checked in sorries in the future.
I like your suggestion to include the warnings to the users, so let me try to add them to your open PR.

While attempting house keeping (deleting some commented out code that had a sorry) I triggered a blueprint build failure that I've never seen before:

  error: no such file or directory (error code: 4294967294)
    file: /home/runner/work/infinity-cosmos/infinity-cosmos/docbuild/.lake/build/doc/style.css
  Some required targets logged failures:
  - InfinityCosmos/InfinityCosmos:docs
  error: build failed
Ah, I've seen this before, it's an issue with the docgen action. It was fixed afaik, but the repo is pinned to an older version. Here: cosmos#212

...which promptly failed on main for other reasons. Unfortunately when this runs on PRs it does not fully exercise the action (this is why it fails only after you merge to main and not before). cosmos#214 should address this: I have tested it on a push in my fork so that it actually ran the full thing, so I'm fairly confident, but we'll see
